title: Preserve endpoint paths and parse URL schemes structurally
description:
## Summary

Both clients strip trailing slashes from the entire supplied URL. This breaks WebSocket negotiation for subtree handlers such as the repository's documented `/wd/` mount. The Go client also changes schemes using unrestricted string replacement, which can modify URL text inside query parameters.

## Affected code

- `client.go:17` calls `strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/")`.
- `client.mjs:33` performs the equivalent regular-expression replacement.
- `client.go:26-27` replaces the first occurrences of `https://` and `http://` anywhere in the string.
- `README.md:25` mounts `/wd/`.
- `README.md:46` and `example/index.html:58` dial `/wd`.

## Reproduction

Mount the server with:

```go
mux.Handle("/wd/", srv)
```

Then force the JavaScript WebSocket transport against `http://host/wd` or even `http://host/wd/`. The client normalizes both to `/wd`; the HTTP mux redirects to `/wd/`, and the WebSocket handshake fails. Auto mode silently falls back to SSE, hiding the loss of the preferred transport.

For Go, a URL such as:

```text
http://host/wd?next=https://example.test/
```

can have the query value rewritten while constructing the WebSocket URL.

## Impact

The documented mounting pattern cannot use forced WebSocket and unexpectedly uses the slower fallback in auto mode. Query corruption can change application-visible parameters or signatures.

## Proposed fix

- Treat the supplied endpoint URL as exact; do not strip its trailing path separator.
- Parse URLs structurally with `net/url` in Go and `URL` in JavaScript.
- Change only the scheme: `http` to `ws`, and `https` to `wss`.
- Build SSE session, ping, and close query parameters through the URL query APIs so existing queries and fragments are handled correctly.
- Update all examples to use the exact mounted `/wd/` endpoint.

## Acceptance criteria

- Forced WS and SSE both work when mounted at `/wd/`.
- Root endpoints, nested paths, existing query parameters, encoded values, IPv6 hosts, and HTTPS URLs are covered by table-driven tests.
- Query values containing `http://` or `https://` remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Go and JavaScript clients follow the same endpoint-preservation rules.
- Auto mode selects WebSocket for the documented server example.
